## What this project is

This repository is the FP26 course project for *Fundamentals of Programming for
Digital Health* (HPI, WS 2026/27). It follows the workflow described on the
course pages: a well-named GitHub repository, a reproducible folder structure,
and a Quarto document that reads its data through helper functions kept in
`functions.py`.

Everything shown here is generated from the code in this repository by running
`quarto render`.

## Repository layout

| Path                  | Purpose                                            |
|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| `main_file.qmd`       | this Quarto document                               |
| `functions.py`        | data handling and plotting helpers                 |
| `data/data_small.csv` | small derived data set, tracked by git             |
| `raw_data_large/`     | large raw data, kept local and listed in `.gitignore` |
| `figures/`            | figures written by the document                    |

## The data

The small table holds heart rate and systolic blood pressure for three
synthetic patients, recorded every four hours over twelve hours.

```{python}
#| label: setup
from pathlib import Path

from functions import by_patient, plot_heart_rate, read_vitals, summarize

Path("figures").mkdir(exist_ok=True)

rows = read_vitals("data/data_small.csv")
print(f"{len(rows)} measurements from {len(by_patient(rows))} patients")
```

## Summary per patient

For each patient, the mean heart rate and its range over the recording:

```{python}
for patient, patient_rows in sorted(by_patient(rows).items()):
    stats = summarize([r["heart_rate"] for r in patient_rows])
    print(
        f"{patient}: n={stats['n']}, mean={stats['mean']:.1f} bpm, "
        f"range {stats['min']:.0f}–{stats['max']:.0f} bpm"
    )
```

## Heart rate over time

```{python}
#| label: fig-heart-rate
#| fig-cap: "Heart rate over the first twelve hours of the recording."

figure = plot_heart_rate(rows, "figures/heart_rate.png")
figure
```

## Reproducing this document

From the repository root:

```bash
quarto render
```

This requires Quarto and Python 3 with `matplotlib` installed.
